props.gloss_en: one who finds kilayim in his garment strips them off even in the marketplace
wherever there is desecration of the Name, one does not show honour to the teacher
the verse for it: 'there is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel against the Lord' (Prov 21:30)
returning from a burial with two paths before them, one pure and one impure: if the mourner goes by the impure one, they go with him by the impure one, for his honour
R' Abba: the baraita speaks of a beit haperas, whose impurity is rabbinic
a person may blow [the dust] through a beit haperas and walk
a beit haperas that has been trodden is pure
R' Elazar bar Tzadok: we [priests] used to jump over the coffins of the dead to greet the kings of Israel
and not only to greet the kings of Israel but even the kings of the nations, so that if one merits he will distinguish between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations
Rava: by Torah law, a tent with a handbreadth of space interposes before impurity
and one without a handbreadth of space does not interpose before impurity
and most coffins have a handbreadth of space
and [the Sages] decreed on those that have [a handbreadth] because of those that do not
and for the honour of kings the Sages did not decree in their case
great is human dignity, which overrides a negative command of the Torah
Rav bar Shaba, before Rav Kahana: the baraita's negative command is the prohibition 'you shall not turn aside' (Deut 17:11)
Rav Kahana: all the words of the Sages were rested on the prohibition 'you shall not turn aside', and for the sake of [human] dignity the Sages permitted
'and hide yourself from them' (Deut 22:1): at times you hide yourself from them, at times you do not
if he was a priest and it [the lost object] is in a cemetery -- for this it says 'and hide yourself'
or he was an elder and it is not in keeping with his dignity -- for this it says 'and hide yourself'
or his own work was worth more than his fellow's [loss] -- for this it says 'and hide yourself'

'and for his sister' -- why stated? one going to slaughter his paschal lamb and circumcise his son who heard that a relative died: might he turn back and become impure? you said: he shall not become impure
might he, as he does not become impure for them, also not become impure for a met mitzva? the verse says 'and for his sister': for his sister he does not become impure
but he does become impure for a met mitzva
